DataCite/Datacite: Points to 4.5 version of DataCite (see https://schema.datacite.org/meta/kernel-4.5)
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite: Points to 4.1 version of DataCite (see https://schema.datacite.org/meta/kernel-4.1)
Recommending changes: No changes recommended: Julian recommends not changing which version of DataCite either export points to

DataCite/Datacite:
From Jim's comparison in June 2024, for the DataCite export's publicationYear element:
- Dataverse uses the year of the date field that the user has set as the citation date, using the API endpoint "Set Citation Date Field Type for a Dataset"
- If the user hasn't set the dataset's citation date using that API endpoint, then the DataCite export uses the latest of:
    - the Publication Date, when the dataset's first version was published in the Dataverse repository or 
    - the embargo citation date, being the latest date of embargoed files on the dataset's first version
- If the latest dataset version is a draft and the user hasn't set any embargo dates for files in the dataset, the DataCite export uses the date when the user last updated the draft version
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite: From Jim's comparison in June 2024, for OpenAIRE export's publicationYear element, Dataverse uses the year of the latest Publication Date, Distribution Date, or Deposit Date.
Recommending changes: Recommending change to OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export: Can the OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export follow the same logic that the DataCite/Datacite export does here?

DataCite/Datacite:
When the user adds an author and any author identifier type (except for DAI), the identifier's URL is included in DataCite's schemeURI property. 

For example:
<nameIdentifier nameIdentifierScheme="ORCID" schemeURI="https://orcid.org">https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9229-5317</nameIdentifier>

<nameIdentifier nameIdentifierScheme="ISNI" schemeURI="http://www.isni.org">http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000121479733</nameIdentifier>
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite:
When the user adds an author and an ORCID identifier type, the identifier's URL is included in a SchemeURI property, instead of DataCite's schemeURI property.

When the user adds an author and any identifier type that is not an ORCID, the identifier's URL is not included in any SchemeURI or schemeURI property.

For example:
<nameIdentifier SchemeURI="https://orcid.org/" nameIdentifierScheme="ORCID">0000-0001-9229-5317</nameIdentifier>

<nameIdentifier nameIdentifierScheme="ISNI">0000000121479733</nameIdentifier>
Recommending changes: Recommending change to OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export: Can the OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export follow the same logic that the DataCite/Datacite export does here? That is, use a property named schemeURI instead of SchemeURI (with a capital S). And use it when the user adds an author and an author identifier type, except for DAI.

DataCite/Datacite: When the user adds an author and a DAI author identifier type and a DAI identifier, the author identifier is not included in DataCite's nameIdentifier property
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite:
When the user adds an author and a DAI author identifier type and a DAI identifier, the author identifier is included in DataCite's nameIdentifier property.

For example:
<nameIdentifier nameIdentifierScheme="DAI">info:eu-repo/dai/nl/072728442</nameIdentifier>
Recommending changes: Recommending change to DataCite/Datacite export: Can the DataCite/Datacite export work in the way that the OpenAIRE/oai_datacite does, so that when the user adds an author and a DAI author identifier type and a DAI identifier, the author identifier is included in DataCite's nameIdentifier property?

DataCite/Datacite:
When the user uses the controlled vocabulary functionality to add a ROR to an author affiliation, the affiliation includes the affiliationIdentifier, schemeURI, and affiliationIdentifierScheme, and the value of the affiliation property is the organization's name.

For example:
<affiliation affiliationIdentifier="https://ror.org/03vek6s52" schemeURI="https://ror.org" affiliationIdentifierScheme="ROR">Harvard University</affiliation>
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite:
When the user uses the controlled vocabulary functionality to add a ROR to an author affiliation, the affiliation does not include the affiliationIdentifier, schemeURI, and affiliationIdentifierScheme, and the value of the affiliation property is the ROR URL.

For example:
<affiliation>https://ror.org/03vek6s52</affiliation>
Recommending changes: Recommending change to OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export: Can the OpenAIRE/oai_datacite export follow the same logic that the DataCite/Datacite export does here?

DataCite/Datacite:
Includes guessed nameTypes (person or organization) when the user chooses any option from Dataverse's Contributor Types dropdown and when the user does not choose an option from the dropdown.

For example:
<contributor contributorType="Producer">
     <contributorName nameType="Personal">Producer Name</contributorName>

Doesn't include guessed nameTypes when the user chooses any of the following options from the Contributor Type dropdown: Producer, Distributor, Editor, Hosting Institution, Project Leader, Project Manager, Project Member, Researcher, Rights Holder, Sponsor, Supervisor, Work Package Leader, and Other

For example:
<contributor contributorType="Producer">
     <contributorName>Producer Name</contributorName>

DataCite/Datacite:
When the user chooses a predefined license, the rights metadata includes rightsIdentifier, rightsIdentifierScheme, schemeURI and xml:lang

For example:
<rights
    rightsURI="http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0" 
    rightsIdentifier="CC0-1.0" 
    rightsIdentifierScheme="SPDX" 
    schemeURI="https://spdx.org/licenses/" 
    xml:lang="en">Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication.
</rights>
OpenAIRE/oai_datacite:

For example:

    rightsURI="http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0">CC0 1.0
</rights>

rightsIdentifier, rightsIdentifierScheme, schemeURI do not exist in DataCite v4.1
